skill.name: code-review-preferences
skill.description: Guide code and pull request reviews with a three-pass method, practical checklists, and constructive feedback standards.
skill.summary: A focused framework for consistent, constructive code reviews.
skill.author: ChaiWithJai

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives. The cited text is a review heading and a test checklist item, with no network activity, reconnaissance instruction, or executable content. No prompt injection or other intent-level security concern was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited lines only introduce a correctness review pass and ask reviewers to consider bugs, edge cases, and security. They contain no network target, command, tool call, or reconnaissance instruction.
The cited lines are a local code-review checklist for passing tests and finding obvious bugs. They do not direct network access or collection of information about external systems.

content.user_title: Improve Code Reviews with Clear Standards
content.value_statement: Inconsistent reviews can miss defects and create unhelpful feedback. This skill uses a three-pass method and focused checklist to guide clear, constructive reviews.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviewers through understanding, correctness, and improvement passes.
Checks code changes for bugs, edge cases, security issues, and exposed secrets.
Limits improvement feedback to five comments per review.
Promotes specific questions and actionable line-level feedback.
Accepts pasted code, referenced files, or a pull request description as review context.
limitations: It does not run tests or inspect a repository unless the AI tool receives that context.
It cannot guarantee that all bugs, vulnerabilities, or breaking changes are found.
Its function-length guideline may not fit every language or architecture.
It provides review guidance, not a substitute for team-specific policies or specialist security review.

use_cases.title: Review a small pull request
use_cases.description: Use the three-pass method to give concise feedback on a focused change.

use_cases.title: Standardize team feedback
use_cases.description: Apply the same checklist and constructive feedback style across team reviews.

use_cases.title: Learn review habits
use_cases.description: Practice identifying correctness concerns before suggesting maintainability improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Review pasted code
prompt_templates.prompt:
Review this code using the three-pass method. Identify correctness issues first, then provide no more than five improvement comments.

[paste code or diff]
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner reviewing a small code change

prompt_templates.title: Review a referenced file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review @filename using this skill's checklist. Focus on bugs, edge cases, security concerns, and clear feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Review a feature pull request
prompt_templates.prompt:
Review this feature change. First explain the intended scope, then check tests, breaking changes, secrets, security, and maintainability. Limit recommendations to the five highest-value comments.

[describe or paste the PR]

prompt_templates.title: Perform a risk-focused review
prompt_templates.prompt:
Perform a risk-focused review of this change. Prioritize correctness, authorization, input validation, error handling, exposed secrets, and regression risk. Separate required fixes from optional improvements.

[paste diff and relevant context]
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a sensitive change

output_examples.input: Review a function that assumes a user record always exists.
output: Correctness: The function can fail when the user record is missing.
Suggestion: Add a guard clause and return a clear not-found result.
Question: What should callers receive when the record is absent?

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that adds a payment retry process.
output: Scope: The change retries failed payment requests.
Required check: Confirm retries are idempotent to prevent duplicate charges.
Required check: Verify failure paths are covered by tests.

best_practices: Understand the change and its scope before writing review comments.
Prioritize correctness, security, and regression risks over personal style preferences.
Make each comment specific, actionable, and respectful.
anti_patterns: Do not use reviews to enforce personal preferences without a team standard.
Do not leave vague feedback without identifying the concern or next step.
Do not overwhelm authors with minor comments when critical issues need attention.

faq.question: What review process does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses three passes: understand the change, check correctness, then suggest improvements.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests?
faq.answer: No. It reminds reviewers to verify tests, but it does not execute them by itself.

faq.question: How many comments should a review contain?
faq.answer: The improvement pass recommends a maximum of five comments to keep feedback focused.

faq.question: Can it review security concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. Its checklist includes security vulnerabilities and secrets, but it is not a full security audit.

faq.question: Can I use a file instead of pasting code?
faq.answer: Yes. Reference a file with @filename when your AI tool supports file context.

faq.question: Is the function length rule mandatory?
faq.answer: No. The under-50-lines guideline is a prompt for discussion, not a universal requirement.
